scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

It's important to assess whether the investment is worthwhile, especially if the fabric won't be used again. 5. **Time Constraints**: Adequate time must be available to purchase the fabric, design an outfit, and have it made before the wedding. Time management is crucial to avoid stress. 6. **Alternative Options**: Exploring alternatives, such as matching colors or similar fabrics, could provide a compromise that respects family traditions while accommodating personal style. 7. **Communication**: Open dialogue with family members can help address concerns and find a compromise, ensuring participation without discomfort. 8. **Significance of the Event**: The wedding's importance to the couple should be considered, potentially outweighing personal inconveniences. 9. **Logistical Challenges**: The ease of sourcing the fabric is a practical consideration. message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did something wrong by giving my girlfriend advice on how to improve her cooking. We've been together for a while, and when we moved in together, we agreed that she would handle the cooking because she gets home earlier from work. At first, I was really happy about this because I got to come home to a hot meal, which was a big change from when I was living alone and often just ate takeout or something quick. But over time, I noticed that her cooking wasn't up to the standard I was used to. It wasn't terrible, and everything was edible, but it just didn't taste as good as what I was used to. I thought, maybe she doesn't know that there's room for improvement, so I started giving her pointers. I tried to be constructive, telling her things like she used too little salt or too much spice, or that something was a little burnt or undercooked. I always made sure to eat everything and say thank you, so I didn't think I was being rude about it. Then, when my mom came to visit, I casually mentioned that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend seemed fine with it at the time, even nodding and smiling. But as soon as my mom left, she went ballistic, accusing me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family. She's been refusing to cook for me ever since, and I apologized, saying I'm sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom, but it didn't calm her down much. I think she's overreacting because I never complained about her cooking or threw it out. I was just trying to be helpful. I miss her cooking, and I'm wondering if I crossed a line somewhere. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) or is my girlfriend just being crazy? Alright, so to break this down, I need to consider a few things. First, communication is key in any relationship, and how I delivered the feedback might have been the issue. Even though I thought I was being constructive, maybe the way I presented it came off as critical or condescending. Also, involving my mom in this might have made her feel like I was comparing her to my family or that I didn't have confidence in her abilities. Another angle is to think about the dynamic of the relationship. We've been together for a while, and moving in together is a big step. Maybe she felt the pressure of taking on the cooking role, and my feedback added to that stress. It's possible that she felt like I wasn't appreciating her efforts, even if I was trying to help. I also need to consider her feelings and how she perceives the situation. She might feel humiliated or insecure about her cooking skills, especially in front of my family. My mom's advice might have been seen as an endorsement of my criticism, making her feel even more self-conscious. On the other hand, I was trying to be helpful and supportive by offering tips to improve her cooking. I didn't mean to hurt her feelings, and I always made sure to eat everything and express gratitude. Maybe I didn't realize how sensitive she was about her cooking, or how much she values her role in preparing meals for our home. It's also worth thinking about how we can move forward. Apologizing was a good start, but maybe I need to have a more open and honest conversation about our expectations and how we can support each other without making either of us feel criticized or insecure. In summary, while my intentions were good, the way I delivered the feedback and involving my mom might have crossed a line. It's important to approach such situations with sensitivity and consider how the other person might feel, especially in a relationship where trust and mutual respect are crucial.
